text:
Mark Scheifele scored with two seconds left in regulation, a power-play slap shot that gave Winnipeg a 4-3 win and ended Tampa Bay's three-game winning streak. The Jets had led 3-0 and watched Pontus Holmberg erase it with two goals 26 seconds apart in the third period, his second a backhand that tied the game at 14:27. Scheifele's winner came off passes from Cole Perfetti and Gabriel Vilardi, and the Jets have now won three straight.

It was also a night for Brayden Yager, the 14th pick in 2023, who scored his first NHL goal on a power-play snap shot that made it 3-0. He put up 82 points in 54 games for Moose Jaw last season, and this one was the first to count at this level.

Our numbers say Winnipeg earned the result. Expected goals, which measure the quality of chances rather than the count of shots, favored the Jets 4.08 to 2.36, and in our simulated replays of every shot they win this game 77% of the time. Tampa Bay had more shot attempts (51 to 44), but Winnipeg blocked 17 of them against just 3 the other way. The power play settled it: the Jets scored on 3 of 5 chances, while the Lightning went 0 for 4. Winnipeg also outchanced Tampa Bay 2.38 to 1.26 in the third, even as the lead disappeared. The Jets carry a three-game winning streak into their next game, and the Lightning head out having lost for the first time after three straight wins.
